message.content:
Build a PERSISTENT, portal-wide terminal dock for the Nxeon customer portal in /opt/nxeon (Next.js 15 App Router, React 19). Today the web terminal (`components/customer/WebTerminal.tsx`, opened by `components/customer/OpenTerminalButton.tsx` and from the Build-with-AI / Claude Code pages) is mounted per-page via `createPortal`. When the user navigates away or closes it, the component unmounts, the websocket dies, and the shell session is lost — they have to reconnect and restart their build. Fix this by lifting the terminal into a single dock mounted at the portal-layout level so the session survives page navigation, with multi-server tabs and a minimize-to-widget mode.

## Read first (do NOT run git; do NOT run `npm run build`)
- `components/customer/WebTerminal.tsx` — the current xterm.js client (token auth → websocket → `terminal-server/index.ts` protocol). Reuse its connection logic verbatim.
- `components/customer/OpenTerminalButton.tsx` — the trigger on the server detail page.
- `app/api/terminal/token/route.ts` and `lib/terminal-token.ts` — how the short-lived WS token is minted (session + ownership check). Reuse unchanged.
- `terminal-server/index.ts` — the WS wire protocol (client→server JSON `{type:"data"|"resize"}`, server→client raw output). Do NOT change the protocol.
- `components/portal/Shell.tsx` — the shared customer/admin portal shell (App Router keeps this mounted across page navigations within the portal, which is the whole point — a component rendered here persists). It was recently given a collapsible sidebar; PRESERVE all of that.
- `app/dashboard/build/page.tsx`, `app/dashboard/claude-code/page.tsx`, `app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx` — the entry points that should open/attach to the dock.

## Architecture (follow this)
1. **`components/customer/terminal/TerminalDock.tsx`** (new, "use client") — a context provider (`TerminalDockProvider`) + the dock UI (`TerminalDock`), plus a `useTerminalDock()` hook exposing `openSession({id, hostname})`, `focusSession(id)`, `closeSession(id)`, `minimize()`, `restore()`, `close()`. Mount `<TerminalDockProvider>` wrapping the Shell's children and render `<TerminalDock/>` once inside Shell (customer portal). It starts inert (nothing visible until a session opens).
2. **Sessions kept alive in refs** — hold an array of open sessions in state for rendering the tab bar, but keep each session's live objects (the xterm `Terminal` instance, its `FitAddon`, and the `WebSocket`) in a `Map` ref so they SURVIVE re-renders and route changes. Opening a server that's already a tab focuses it instead of duplicating.
3. **Persistent xterm DOM** — the hard part: each session's xterm must keep its scrollback + live socket when the dock switches between maximized and the minimized widget, and when the user changes pages. Do this by giving each session its own persistent container `<div>` (created once, stored in the ref Map). Render all session containers in the dock; show only the active one (`display:none` the others — their sockets stay connected in the background). Call `fitAddon.fit()` on show/resize and send a `resize` message. Because the dock lives in Shell, page navigation never unmounts it, so sockets persist. Do NOT recreate the Terminal/WebSocket on focus or restore.
4. **Tabs** — a tab bar across the top of the dock: one tab per connected server (hostname + status dot + close ✕), and a **"+" button** that opens a small picker of the user's *running* servers to add another tab (connect to multiple servers at once). For the picker's server list, add a tiny server action (e.g. in a new `lib/actions-terminal.ts`, `"use server"`, `listTerminalServers()` → requireUser → the caller's RUNNING servers as `{id, hostname}[]`); call it when the picker opens. Exclude servers already open as tabs.
5. **Minimize widget** — a "minimize" control shrinks the dock to a small floating terminal widget pinned **bottom-center** (`fixed bottom-4 left-1/2 -translate-x-1/2`, ~460×280, above other widgets with a sensible z-index), still showing the live active session (keystrokes keep working). Clicking it (a restore/expand control) brings back the full dock. A "close" ✕ tears down that session's socket + xterm; closing the last session hides the dock entirely.
6. **Wire the triggers** — `OpenTerminalButton` becomes a thin button that calls `useTerminalDock().openSession(...)` (no more local `<WebTerminal>`; you may keep WebTerminal for reference or delete it if fully replaced — if you delete it, update every importer). The Build-with-AI and Claude Code pages' "open terminal / start building" affordance should also call `openSession` (via a small client trigger component if those pages are server components). After opening, the user can navigate anywhere in the portal and the session stays connected + running.

## Styling / behavior
- Match the existing dark Nxeon theme and the current WebTerminal's look (same xterm theme, `card`/`btn-*`/border tokens). The maximized dock should be a large bottom sheet or right slide-in that does NOT cover the sidebar; the minimized widget is the small bottom-center pill/panel.
- Keep it desktop-first; on mobile it can be a simple full-width sheet. Respect that Feedback + chat widgets already sit at bottom-right — the minimized terminal at bottom-center must not overlap them.
- Persist which sessions are open across reloads is NOT required (sockets can't survive a full reload); persistence is about in-app navigation, which the Shell-level mount gives you for free.

## Constraints
- No new npm deps (xterm/addon-fit already present). Do NOT change `terminal-server/index.ts`, the token route, or `lib/terminal-token.ts`. Do NOT touch `prisma/schema.prisma`. Do NOT run git or `npm run build`.
- PRESERVE the Shell's collapsible-sidebar behavior and all gates/badges — only ADD the provider wrapper + dock render.
- Write/Edit may intermittently time out on a hook — fall back to `Bash` heredocs and verify files exist.
- Verify ONLY with `cd /opt/nxeon && npx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 | grep -v "test/.*test.ts"` (must be clean for your files).

Report: the new files, exactly how the dock is mounted in Shell, how xterm/ws instances survive navigation and minimize/restore, how the "+" picker + tabs work, and which triggers now call `openSession`.

content.thinking:
I'm mapping out the implementation strategy: I need to create a server action for listing terminal servers and a new terminal dock component with a provider, then integrate them into the Shell component and update the OpenTerminalButton to use the new session handler.

But I'm realizing Shell is shared between both customer and admin portals, so I need to conditionally mount the provider and dock only for customers based on the user's role. The hook will be called by components that are already customer-only (OpenTerminalButton and ClaudeCodeHub), so the provider needs to wrap those specific areas rather than the entire Shell.

Actually, the simplest approach is to always wrap the provider around Shell's children and always render the dock — it'll just stay invisible when there are no open sessions, which is fine for the admin portal since admins never trigger the open action anyway. Since the dock uses fixed positioning, the DOM placement doesn't affect layout, but it must stay inside the provider. I'll wrap the entire Shell return with TerminalDockProvider, placing the children and dock together so that any page calling useTerminalDock can access the context, and the dock persists across navigation.

For gating to customers only, I'll check `user.role === "CUSTOMER"` before rendering TerminalDock itself, while keeping the provider always present since it's harmless and ensures the hook stays safe even if admin portal doesn't use the dock.

Now I'm designing the TerminalDock component. I need a session model that tracks metadata like id, hostname, and connection status separately from the live session objects that hold the actual terminal instance, WebSocket, and DOM references. The provider will manage both a sessions array for the tab bar and state for the active session, display mode, and other UI controls.

For opening sessions, I'll check if one already exists in the map and focus it, otherwise create a new live session with a persistent container div. The tricky part is keeping xterm's DOM element alive across React re-renders — I'll store the container in a ref Map and render those persistent divs into the dock using a portal-like approach.

The cleanest way is to have the dock render a wrapper div for each session with a ref callback that mounts the persistent container into it. Since the container is created once and stored in the map, React manages the wrapper but the child container persists across re-renders.

When switching between maximized and minimized layouts, the ref callback runs again with `null` and then with the new wrapper element, re-appending the same container to preserve the xterm terminal's state and socket connection.

Instead of remounting the wrappers on layout changes, I'll keep a single dock root whose CSS classes control the size and visibility based on the current mode — this way the terminal wrappers stay mounted and xterm never gets disrupted.

For rendering, I only return null when there are no sessions; closing the last session empties the array and hides the dock naturally. The outer container uses fixed positioning with responsive classes to create a bottom sheet that doesn't overlap the sidebar on larger screens.

The challenge is that the sidebar can collapse to a narrower width, and the dock needs to account for that. ## Summary

Built a persistent, portal-wide terminal dock. The shell session now survives in-portal navigation, supports multi-server tabs, and has a minimize-to-widget mode.

### New files
- **`/opt/nxeon/components/customer/terminal/TerminalDock.tsx`** — `"use client"`. Exports `TerminalDockProvider`, the `TerminalDock` UI (rendered by the provider), and the `useTerminalDock()` hook exposing `openSession({id,hostname})`, `focusSession(id)`, `closeSession(id)`, `minimize()`, `restore()`, `close()`.
- **`/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-terminal.ts`** — `"use server"` `listTerminalServers()` → `requireUser()` then the caller's RUNNING servers as `{id,hostname}[]`, for the "+" picker.

### How it's mounted in Shell
`/opt/nxeon/components/portal/Shell.tsx` imports `TerminalDockProvider` and wraps its entire return in `<TerminalDockProvider>…</TerminalDockProvider>`. The provider renders `<TerminalDock/>` internally (once), so the dock lives at the shell level. Because App Router keeps Shell mounted across page changes, the dock and its sockets are never unmounted. The provider is inert (renders `null`) until a page calls `openSession`, so it's harmless in the admin portal too. All sidebar/collapse/gate/badge logic in Shell is untouched — only the wrapper was added.

### How xterm/ws survive navigation + minimize/restore
- Tab-bar metadata (`{id, hostname, status}`) lives in `sessions` state; the live objects (xterm `Terminal`, `FitAddon`, `WebSocket`, `ResizeObserver`, and a persistent container `<div>`) live in a `Map` ref (`liveRef`) that React never recreates.
- Each session's xterm is opened into its own persistent container div (created once in `openSession`, stored in the ref). The dock renders one mount slot per session; a ref callback (`attach`) appends that same div into the slot and kicks off `connect()` only if the session has no terminal yet. Switching tabs just toggles `display`; hidden sessions keep their sockets open.
- Minimize/restore only swaps the outer wrapper's size/position CSS classes (`fixed bottom-0 inset-x-0 lg:left-60` bottom sheet vs. `fixed bottom-4 left-1/2 -translate-x-1/2` ~460×280 widget) — the terminal-surface subtree keeps the same DOM nodes, so nothing is recreated. `fitAndResize` is called via a ResizeObserver per session plus a `requestAnimationFrame` effect on `activeId`/`mode` change, sending a `resize` message on show. Connection logic (token → `wss /terminal-ws` → JSON `{type:"data"|"resize"}`) is reused verbatim from WebTerminal; the protocol, token route, and `terminal-token.ts` are unchanged.

### Tabs + "+" picker
Tab bar across the top: one tab per server (status dot + hostname + per-tab ✕ that tears down that session's socket/xterm). A "+" button opens a popover that calls `listTerminalServers()` and lists RUNNING servers excluding ones already open as tabs; clicking one calls `openSession`. Opening a server that's already a tab focuses it instead of duplicating. Right-side controls: minimize/restore toggle and a dock-close ✕; closing the last session hides the dock. A reconnect strip appears when the active session's socket drops. The minimized widget is pinned bottom-center (`z-[65]`) to avoid the bottom-right Feedback/chat widgets; the maximized sheet (`z-[70]`, `lg:left-60`) does not cover the sidebar.

### Triggers now calling openSession
- `/opt/nxeon/components/customer/OpenTerminalButton.tsx` — rewritten as a thin button calling `useTerminalDock().openSession(...)` (server detail page, unchanged call site).
- `/opt/nxeon/components/customer/claude-code/ClaudeCodeHub.tsx` — "Open terminal & start building" now calls `openSession`; removed the local `<WebTerminal>` and its `terminalOpen` state.
- `/opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/build/page.tsx` — added an `OpenTerminalButton` in the header (shown when usable and a running server exists).

`WebTerminal.tsx` was left in place for reference (no remaining importers).
